analysis_steps.goal: Image and characterise continuum and CO lines

method.value: CLEAN imaging, 2D Gaussian fit to continuum, moment maps of 12CO and C18O

evidence.quote: its deconvolved size can be estimated from a 2D Gaussian fitting

analysis_steps.goal: Measure rotation profile from major-axis PV diagram

method.value: Intensity-weighted mean position per channel (>6 sigma) on PV along disk major axis (PA 73 deg); double power-law chi2 fit in log R - log V

evidence.quote: We performed a $\chi^{2}$ fitting to Fig. [9](#fig:ll) with a double power model

key_parameters.value: mean positions not measured for |dV|<1.2 km/s; Vsys=6.4 km/s

evidence.quote: The mean position is not measured at low velocities ($|\Delta V|<1.2\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$)

assumptions.value: errors: Gaussian for log R, rectangular for log V

evidence.quote: We adopted a Gaussian distribution for the error of $\log R$ and a rectangular distribution for the error of $\log V$

fitting.value: chi2 with Monte Carlo dispersal of points within errors; compared with single power law

evidence.quote: The error of each parameter is derived by dispersing the data points randomly within the error bars of $\log R$ and $\log V$.

validation.value: reduced chi2 1.6 (double) vs 2.0 (single); resolution bias analysed in Appendix

evidence.quote: giving reduced $\chi^{2}=1.6$

analysis_steps.goal: Fit Keplerian disk model to high-velocity C18O channel maps

method.value: 3D LTE radiative transfer disk model, MCMC chi2 minimisation on pixels >3 sigma with |dV|>2.4 km/s

evidence.quote: We use Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) method to find the minimum $\chi^{2}$ efficiently.

software: MCMC (unnamed code of Ohashi et al. 2014)

evidence.quote: fixed | $i$ | $R_{\rm in}$ | $R_{\rm out}$

fitting.value: reduced chi2 minimisation; uncertainties from range where chi2 < min+1

evidence.quote: The uncertainty of each parameter is defined by the range of the parameter where the reduced $\chi^{2}$ is below the minimum plus one

evidence.quote: indicating that C$^{18}$O traces mainly a flattened envelope surrounding the disk and the central protostar

claims.result: p_in=0.54±0.14 and v=0.53 with M*=0.68 Msun

evidence.quote: This indicates that the rotation at higher velocities can be explained as Keplerian rotation orbiting a protostar with a dynamical mass of $0.68\ M_{\odot}$

claims.experiment: Compare FE/SE model PV diagrams with observations

why_this_method.value: PV analysis along major axis avoids contamination from outflow/infall; channel-map fit restricted to rotation-dominated velocities

evidence.quote: it is required that only the velocity channels where rotation is dominant should be used for comparison with a disk model.

limitations_admitted.value: Inclination poorly constrained by the disk model; mass estimates are uncertain by optical depth, temperature, abundance

evidence.quote: it is difficult to give a constraint on the inclination angle in this model fitting

limitations_admitted.value: PV mean-position method underestimates break radius at limited resolution

evidence.quote: may systematically underestimate $R_{b}$ when the spatial resolution is not high enough

referee_caveats_inferred: Single ~1 arcsec resolution observation; disk (~100 AU) barely resolved
Inclination degenerate, so M* and infall factor depend on assumed 65 deg
Flattened-envelope model fit by eye with no uncertainties on alpha
Dust mass opacity values inconsistent between text and conclusions
12CO resolved out near systemic velocity; missing short spacings affect low-velocity infall signature
